description: Rove is a voice troubleshooting agent for a consumer dash-cam line. A React page joins a LiveKit room; a Python agent worker in the FastAPI process hears the caller (Amazon Transcribe), decides when the turn has ended, and speaks (Amazon Polly). Every turn runs through a LangGraph state machine that retrieves Tier-1 chunks from Postgres plus pgvector, filters the legal next steps in code, lets a Bedrock Nova model choose among them, and passes the result through a deterministic output guard. The corpus is built offline by ingest/, the whole system is scored by three eval harnesses, an https page reaches the media server through a same-origin wss relay, and a separate support console can join a live session.

components.name: React Client
components.description: The browser page (Vite + React 18, `livekit-client` as the only runtime dependency besides React). It renders a projection of the server's diagnostic state in four panels and offers click-or-type next to the voice channel. It never owns state: a reload loses nothing.

components.name: Session Control Plane
components.description: One WebSocket plus the REST calls that start it. `api.js` mints the session and renews the token; `useSession` holds the state projection the panels render from.

components.name: Media Links
components.description: The two media legs. `LiveKitLink` joins a LiveKit room with the minted token (the default transport); `MediaLink` is the Pipecat SmallWebRTC fallback. `summariseStats` turns browser `getStats()` into the RTT, jitter and loss numbers the page shows and the trace records.

components.name: Panels and Page
components.description: `App` lays out transcript, current step, diagnostic state and connection bar. Each panel is a small component; `Composer` is the click-or-type input and `EventLog` shows the live trace.

components.name: FastAPI Server
components.description: One FastAPI process on one port. It mints short-lived session credentials, serves the built client, owns the control WebSocket, runs every typed turn against the diagnostic core, and holds consent, handoff, trace and transcript records. In the default transport it does not carry media.

components.name: App and Settings
components.description: `create_app` assembles the routes (`/healthz`, `/api/session`, `/api/session/{room}/token`, `/api/offer`, `/api/ice`, `/api/trace/{room}`, `/ws`), the static client, the `/support` console and the support routes, and, under the livekit transport, `/lk`. `/api/offer` and `/api/ice` serve only the Pipecat fallback. `Settings` reads every option from the environment; `main` runs uvicorn.

components.name: Session Credentials
components.description: Mints and verifies the short-lived, single-room, single-identity tokens. `livekit_tokens` is the JWT the LiveKit media server accepts; `tokens` is the earlier token for the Pipecat fallback.

components.name: Turn Bridge
components.description: The click-or-type path and the session registry. A click, a typed string and a transcribed utterance enter as the same event; `run_typed_turn` calls `agent.core.diagnose`, `fanout` pushes the result to every participant.

components.name: Consent, Handoff and Records
components.description: Per-session consent, the escalation handoff rendered from `DiagnosticState`, the per-session JSONL trace, and consented transcripts written to Postgres (`pilot_sessions`, `pilot_transcript_lines`).

components.name: Server Verifier
components.description: `python -m server.verify` starts a server, checks the mint, the media path, the trace and a typed turn, then stops it.

components.name: LiveKit Voice Pipeline
components.description: The media path in production: an agent worker that joins the LiveKit room as a participant, with Silero VAD, context-dependent endpointing, streaming Amazon Transcribe, incremental Amazon Polly, speculative prefetch and a latency ladder. A Pipecat SmallWebRTC path is kept as a documented fallback.

components.name: Agent Worker
components.description: `AgentWorker` runs the LiveKit worker; `entrypoint` joins a room; `RoomVoiceAgent` owns one room's audio loop, barge-in and turn dispatch.

components.name: Endpointing
components.description: Decides end-of-turn with a hangover chosen by FSM state rather than one global silence threshold.

components.name: Streaming ASR
components.description: Amazon Transcribe Streaming with custom-vocabulary biasing; emits partials that the prefetch consumes.

components.name: Incremental TTS
components.description: Amazon Polly Neural: whole-utterance synthesis with a disk cache, and clause-by-clause incremental synthesis.

components.name: Speculative Prefetch
components.description: On a category-bearing ASR partial of enough words, runs retrieval early and discards the result if the final transcript disagrees.

components.name: Latency and Ladder
components.description: Measures the nine-component latency budget per turn and applies the graded degradation ladder on a measured breach.

components.name: Dev Media Server and Headless Peers
components.description: Runs `livekit-server --dev` locally, joins rooms without a browser, and verifies the voice path end to end (`python -m server.verify_livekit`).

components.name: Pipecat Fallback
components.description: The Pipecat SmallWebRTC peer connection inside the server process (`/api/offer`), its headless test peer, and the ICE-candidate rewrite for hosts behind 1:1 NAT.

components.name: LangGraph Diagnostic Core
components.description: The `agent` package: a typed `DiagnosticState`, a LangGraph `StateGraph` whose nodes are authored step functions, a next-step policy that removes illegal moves before the model sees a candidate list, a Bedrock Nova wrapper, and a deterministic output guard. `core.diagnose(utterance, state)` is the entry point.

components.name: Diagnostic State
components.description: The typed record the policy reads instead of the transcript: 13 FSM states, five interrupts, the attempted-step ledger, hypotheses, device identification.

components.name: State Graph
components.description: The LangGraph `StateGraph`: routing functions, an in-memory checkpointer, and `run_turn` / `resume_turn`.

components.name: Step Functions and Output Guard
components.description: One function per FSM state, `diagnose` as the entry point, and `output_guard`, the last deterministic check before text is spoken or rendered.

components.name: Next-Step Policy
components.description: Produces the legal candidate set: hazard stop, no-repeat, model clearance, destructive gate; also decides escalation.

components.name: Answers and Symptom Coverage
components.description: `answers.py` stores what the caller said in reply to a question as typed data; `symptoms.py` tells a genuine route apart from a nearest-category force.

components.name: Bedrock LLM
components.description: A thin boto3 wrapper: `classify` on Nova Micro, `decide` on Nova Pro, plus `NullLLM` for model-free runs.

components.name: Step Ontology
components.description: The canonical step ids and the taxonomy-id to candidate-step map. It lives in the `eval/` package but is imported by the runtime core, policy, state and server.

components.name: Hybrid Retrieval
components.description: Filter first, then search. `retrieval.retrieve` applies model, category and speakable filters, fuses BM25 and dense scores, reranks and returns the top three Tier-1 chunks. The chunk store is Postgres plus pgvector (Titan embeddings); a JSONL backend takes over when Postgres does not answer.

components.name: Filter, Fuse and Rerank
components.description: The retrieval chain over a `Backend`: model filter (confirmed / probable / unknown), fusion of lexical and dense scores, rerank, top 3 with chunk ids.

components.name: Retrieval Backends
components.description: `PostgresBackend` runs the filter and both halves of the search as SQL; `JsonlBackend` serves `data/processed/chunks.jsonl` with stdlib BM25; `default_backend` picks one once.

components.name: Postgres and pgvector Store
components.description: Schema (`source_registry`, `chunks`, `chunk_lexemes`, `lexeme_df`, `corpus_stats`, `embedding_model`, `chunk_embeddings`), the migration that loads the corpus, Titan embedding calls, and the SQL halves of the hybrid search.

components.name: RAG Corpus and Ingest
components.description: The offline path that builds the Tier-1 corpus: `python -m ingest.run` chunks the saved manuals and help-center pages under `data/raw/` and `data/text/`, attaches metadata and the source registry, and writes `data/processed/chunks.jsonl` and `data/processed/sources.json`. `agent.store.migrate` loads those into Postgres. Tier-2 and Tier-3 collection scripts live in `scripts/` and never feed the speech path.

components.name: Corpus Validation
components.description: `python -m ingest.validate` checks the corpus against the design rules; breaches exit non-zero.

components.name: Known-Issue Watch
components.description: A watcher over public pages whose output is asserted to be Tier 2; it is not a vendor feed and is never speakable.

components.name: Eval Harnesses
components.description: The 30-scenario golden set (`eval/scenarios.json`) scored three ways: Harness A (text, single turn), Harness B (scripted multi-turn) and Harness C (synthesised speech through a real LiveKit room), plus grounding, latency-ladder and prefetch measurements and the two-grader pack with Cohen's kappa.

components.name: Harness A
components.description: Single turn: pre-populates a `DiagnosticState` from the scenario, calls the agent once, scores the next step. `baseline.py` is the deliberately dumb floor agent.

components.name: Harness B
components.description: Scripted multi-turn: a deterministic responder plays the user down each branch.

components.name: Harness C
components.description: End to end spoken: synthesised speech with road noise, injected at real-time pace through a real LiveKit participant, with an ASR-corruption pass.

components.name: Grounding and Grader Pack
components.description: Structural grounding rate from the output guard's verdicts, the two-grader pack, and Cohen's kappa scoring.

components.name: Prefetch and Ladder Measurements
components.description: Replays that measure what speculative prefetch is worth and drive the degradation ladder until it fires and recovers.

components_relations.relation: runs the core over Harness A and captures guard verdicts

components.name: HTTPS and wss Relay
components.description: A page served over https may not open `ws://`, and `livekit-server` does not terminate TLS on its signalling port. When the server runs with `ROVE_TLS_CERT` and `ROVE_TLS_KEY`, uvicorn terminates TLS and `/lk` relays only the signalling (`rtc` paths) to `settings.livekit_url` (default `ws://127.0.0.1:7880`). Media stays browser to media server. A testing-only certificate script and a headless wss verifier ship with it.

components.name: wss Signalling Relay
components.description: `register_livekit_relay` mounts `/lk/{path}` as a WebSocket and HTTP pass-through; only `rtc` and `rtc/...` paths (signalling and its validate probe) are forwarded to `settings.livekit_url`; anything else is closed with 1008.

components.name: TLS Testing Server
components.description: `scripts/serve_https_testing.sh` generates a throwaway CA and leaf certificate under `server/testing-tls/` and starts `python -m server` with `ROVE_TLS_CERT` and `ROVE_TLS_KEY`. Testing only. In `server/config.py`, `Settings.scheme` and `Settings.livekit_public_url` decide whether the page is handed `wss://<host>/lk`.

components.name: wss Verifier
components.description: `python -m server.verify_wss` mints through the https page, asserts the browser would receive `wss://<host>/lk`, and joins a room through it.
